lines.speaker: Minos
lines.text: Let this robber Sostratus here be thrown into the Pyriphlegethon, the temple-robber torn apart by the Chimera, and the tyrant, Hermes, stretched out next to Tityos to have his liver pecked by the vultures as well. But you good ones, go quickly to the Elysian Fields and the Islands of the Blessed to live there, since you did what was right in life.

lines.speaker: Sostratus
lines.text: Listen, Minos, if what I'm about to say seems fair to you.

lines.speaker: Minos
lines.text: Listen again? Haven't you already been shown up as a villain, Sostratus, and killed that many people?

lines.speaker: Sostratus
lines.text: Shown up, sure. But let's see if I deserve to be punished for it.

lines.speaker: Minos
lines.text: Of course, if paying the penalty is the just thing.

lines.speaker: Sostratus
lines.text: Answer me anyway, Minos. It's just one quick question.

lines.speaker: Minos
lines.text: Go on, then. Keep it short—we still have the others to judge.

lines.speaker: Sostratus
lines.text: Everything I did in life—did I do it of my own free will, or was it fated by the Moira?

lines.speaker: Sostratus
lines.text: So all the good people and us so-called bad ones were just carrying out her orders when we did those things?

lines.speaker: Minos
lines.text: Yes. Clotho assigns to each person at birth what they're supposed to do.

lines.speaker: Sostratus
lines.text: Then if someone is forced by another to kill someone—can't argue, just following orders, like an executioner obeying a judge or a bodyguard obeying a tyrant—who do you blame for the murder?

lines.speaker: Minos
lines.text: Obviously the judge or the tyrant. Not even the sword itself counts; it's just a tool doing what the one who gave the order wanted.

lines.speaker: Sostratus
lines.text: Good point, Minos. You're even giving me extra examples. Now, if a servant is sent by his master with gold or silver, who gets the credit? Who's the benefactor?

lines.speaker: Minos
lines.text: The one who sent him, Sostratus. The carrier's just the messenger.

lines.speaker: Sostratus
lines.text: So you see how unfair it is to punish us for being the servants of what Clotho ordered, while you reward the ones who got others to do their dirty work? No one can say we had any choice in the matter when we were under total compulsion.

lines.speaker: Minos
lines.text: Sostratus, if you look closely, you'll find plenty of other things in this place that don't make logical sense. But you've earned yourself a pass with this little argument of yours. You seem to be more than just a robber—you're a bit of a sophist too. Hermes, let him go. No punishment for him. And don't you go teaching the rest of the dead to ask questions like that.
